tasks.title: Document live CLI build prerequisites
tasks.summary: Make the live-test documentation explicit that cross-crate CLI live tests execute target/debug/covenant and therefore require cargo build -p covenant before targeted live runs.
expectedFailureModes: A targeted live CLI test uses a stale target/debug/covenant binary.
Operators run the documented command and get a misleading unknown-command failure.
The full quick gate passes while an isolated live CLI command fails because the binary prerequisite is implicit.
tasks.nextAction: Document the cargo build -p covenant prerequisite for targeted live CLI tests and update public live coverage docs.

tasks.title: Define capability scope schemas
tasks.summary: Specify stable scope payload shapes for each capability action namespace before enforcing more granular signed permissions in code.
expectedFailureModes: Capability scopes remain arbitrary JSON with no compatibility contract.
Future code enforcement rejects existing grants because no schema migration path exists.
Public docs imply scoped permissions are stronger than the current implementation can prove.
tasks.nextAction: Write the capability scope schema contract and mark any enforcement gaps explicitly.

tasks.title: Define audit root signing policy
tasks.summary: Record the first public policy for signing audit roots and publishing verifiable provenance without overclaiming immutable transparency.
expectedFailureModes: Audit integrity remains local-only while docs imply public verifiability.
Signing identity, key rotation, and root subject formats are left ambiguous.
Release artifacts cannot tie audit roots to task and commit provenance.
tasks.nextAction: Add an architecture decision record for audit root signing and update status/docs to match.

tasks.title: Document repeatable Linux gVisor runner setup
tasks.summary: Document the repeatable Linux host prerequisites for the opt-in runsc/rootfs live sandbox test before making stronger sandbox claims.
expectedFailureModes: The gVisor live test exists but cannot be reproduced by contributors.
Sandbox status claims outpace the tested Linux environment.
Rootfs, runsc, and environment variable prerequisites are scattered across test code.
tasks.nextAction: Write the repeatable Linux gVisor live-test runner guide and link it from runtime sandbox docs.

tasks.title: Let autonomy-next seed a backlog task
tasks.summary: When every tracked task is integrated or blocked, let autonomy-next optionally seed the next backlog template so autonomous runs can continue without a separate continuation pass.
expectedFailureModes: Automation dead-ends on autonomy-next even though a backlog template exists.
Seeding produces an invalid task JSON record or bypasses autonomy validation.
Seed mode mutates the task directory without leaving durable evidence in events.
tasks.nextAction: Add a seed option to autonomy-next, document it, and ensure it keeps autonomy state consistent when invoked in a clean worktree.

tasks.title: Add actor metadata when seeding tasks
tasks.summary: Allow autonomy-seed-next to record which role seeded a task and why, so events.jsonl can be audited without guessing the actor or intent.
expectedFailureModes: Seed events all look identical, obscuring whether they were seeded by a planner or an automation loop.
Invalid role strings are accepted and break autonomy validation later.
Notes capture machine-local identifiers that should never land in public history.
tasks.nextAction: Teach autonomy-seed-next to accept --actor and --note flags and apply them to the recorded seed event.

tasks.title: Implement audit root signature generation
tasks.summary: Add deterministic signing and verification for audit-root-attestation.v1 payloads so provenance claims can be verified end-to-end without overclaiming public transparency.
expectedFailureModes: Signatures are generated but the signature metadata format is underspecified and breaks across versions.
Verification accepts malformed payloads or incorrect subjects, undermining the trust boundary.
Docs overclaim public verifiability when keys are still local-only and not rotated.
tasks.nextAction: Choose the signing identity and key format, implement signing + verification, and record the security review notes before integration.

tasks.title: Validate capability scopes at grant time
tasks.summary: Validate versioned capability scope payloads when creating grants so enforcement can be strict without breaking existing callers or accepting arbitrary JSON.
expectedFailureModes: Invalid scope payloads are accepted and later cause enforcement-time failures.
A stricter validator rejects existing persisted grants without a migration path.
Docs imply scoped permissions are enforced even when validation is still permissive.
tasks.nextAction: Define the minimal accepted schema per capability, validate on grant creation, and track any compatibility gaps explicitly.

tasks.title: Add JSON output to peers list
tasks.summary: Add a `--json` flag to `covenant peers list` so tooling and live tests can consume a stable machine-readable shape without parsing tab-delimited human output.
expectedFailureModes: Live tests parse `peers list` output and extract the wrong token prefix or pubkey when rendering changes.
`--json` output omits `truncated` context, causing operators to assume the result set is exhaustive.
JSON output accidentally leaks token bytes, private key material, or other redacted peer registry fields.
tasks.nextAction: Implement `covenant peers list --json`, update the live tests that currently parse human output, and document the machine output contract.

tasks.title: Add JSON output to peers revoke
tasks.summary: Add a `--json` flag to `covenant peers revoke` so automation can distinguish Revoked/AlreadyRevoked/NotFound/Ambiguous without scraping stderr.
expectedFailureModes: Automation scripts scrape stderr and misclassify ambiguous matches as success.
`--json` output changes exit codes or mixes human + JSON output, breaking parsers.
JSON output includes full token bytes or other redacted registry data.
tasks.nextAction: Implement `covenant peers revoke --json` with a stable outcome schema and keep human output unchanged by default.

tasks.title: Cover peers list JSON output in live tests
tasks.summary: Add an opt-in live CLI test that asserts `covenant peers list --json` returns a stable shape and that `truncated` behaves consistently with `--limit`.
expectedFailureModes: The JSON schema drifts without notice, breaking scripts that rely on it.
The CLI prints JSON to stdout but also emits human hints, producing invalid JSON.
`truncated` is incorrect when the daemon returns fewer rows than the limit but still had more peers available.
tasks.nextAction: Add live coverage for `--json` output and update the coverage matrix to point at the new test file.

tasks.title: Cover peers revoke JSON output in live tests
tasks.summary: Add opt-in live CLI coverage for `covenant peers revoke --json` across the NotFound, Ambiguous, and SelfRevokeForbidden outcomes, ensuring the CLI never mixes human stderr with JSON stdout in JSON mode.
expectedFailureModes: JSON mode prints human hints to stderr, breaking automation that expects clean JSON output.
Ambiguous-match JSON leaks more peer registry data than the human output (token bytes, full tokens, or local paths).
Exit codes diverge between human and JSON modes, causing scripts to misclassify failures as success.
tasks.nextAction: Add the live JSON revoke test and update the coverage matrix/docs to reference it.

tasks.title: Enforce peer capability scope predicates
tasks.summary: Define and enforce stable peer scope predicates so `peers.list`, `peers.revoke`, `peers.rotate`, and related dispatch paths cannot act on peers outside the signed scope metadata.
expectedFailureModes: A scoped `peers.revoke` grant can revoke a different peer than the signed selector.
A scoped `peers.list` grant can enumerate peers outside the signed scope, leaking metadata.
Docs imply scoped peer permissions are enforced when dispatch still treats peer scope fields as compatibility metadata.
tasks.nextAction: Write the peer scope predicate contract, implement enforcement in covenantd, and add focused tests for scope mismatch rejections.

tasks.title: Enforce settlement capability scope predicates
tasks.summary: Define and enforce stable settlement scope predicates so receipt reads and batch operations are constrained by signed scope metadata before expanding on-chain claims.
expectedFailureModes: Settlement grants remain effectively unscoped and allow arbitrary receipt reads or batch creation.
Future enforcement rejects existing grants because no explicit schema or migration path exists.
Public docs overclaim settlement isolation before dispatch-time predicates exist.
tasks.nextAction: Write settlement scope schema, implement dispatch checks for receipt reads and batch operations, and add tests that assert scope mismatches are rejected.

tasks.title: Add protocol info compatibility fixtures
tasks.summary: Lock protocol_info wire compatibility with explicit JSON fixtures and tests so stale clients can probe IPC/HTTP version metadata without guessing schema drift.
expectedFailureModes: A refactor changes protocol_info JSON keys and stale clients break during the unauthenticated probe.
Newer daemons add required protocol info fields without defaults, causing older CLIs to fail deserializing the probe response.
Docs describe protocol negotiation while leaving compatibility rules implicit, leading to accidental breaking changes.
verification: cd agent-os && cargo test -p covenantd protocol_info --locked
tasks.nextAction: Add protocol_info JSON fixtures for IPC and HTTP /version, enforce them in tests, and document the compatibility contract for clients.

tasks.title: Add JSON output for recent capabilities
tasks.summary: Add stable machine-readable output for `covenant capabilities recent --json` so autonomous supervisors can inspect delegated authority without parsing human text.
expectedFailureModes: Automation depends on the human arrow/bracket rendering of capability rows.
`--json` emits more than one object or drops signature data needed for audit correlation.
The live CLI surface only tests text output, leaving the machine-readable contract unpinned.
tasks.nextAction: Add `capabilities recent --json`, live subprocess coverage, docs, and stable shape tests.

tasks.title: Add JSON output for capability purge
tasks.summary: Add stable machine-readable output for `covenant capabilities purge --json` so supervisors can run retention maintenance without parsing human text.
expectedFailureModes: Retention automation parses `purged N revoked capability(ies)` and breaks on wording changes.
`--json` omits the cutoff used for the purge, making maintenance receipts hard to correlate.
Live capability coverage keeps grant/recent/revoke only and never exercises retention commands through a real daemon.
tasks.nextAction: Add `capabilities purge --json`, stable shape tests, live subprocess coverage, and docs.

tasks.title: Add JSON output for tools list
tasks.summary: Add stable machine-readable output for `covenant tools list --json` so agents can enumerate tool cards without parsing human text.
expectedFailureModes: Automation depends on human `name — description` rendering and breaks when punctuation changes.
`--json` emits multiple objects or mixes human stdout with JSON output.
The machine-readable tool list diverges from the daemon registry because the CLI applies extra filtering or formatting.
verification: cd agent-os && cargo test -p covenant --locked tool_list_json
cd agent-os && cargo test -p covenantd --test live_cli_tools_list_json --locked -- --ignored live_
tasks.nextAction: Add `tools list --json`, a stable tool_list shape test, and an ignored live CLI JSON round trip.

tasks.title: Add JSON output for ignore checks
tasks.summary: Add stable machine-readable output for `covenant ignore check --json` so automation can gate prompts on `.covenantignore` without parsing human text.
expectedFailureModes: Automation parses `ignored — matched rule:` and breaks when punctuation changes.
`--json` changes exit codes (ignored should remain non-zero) and breaks gating logic.
The JSON output omits the matched pattern or rules_loaded fields required for debugging.
verification: cd agent-os && cargo test -p covenant --locked ignore_report_json
cd agent-os && cargo test -p covenantd --test live_cli_ignore_check_json --locked -- --ignored live_
tasks.nextAction: Add `ignore check --json`, keep exit codes, add a stable shape unit test, and update CLI docs.

tasks.title: Add JSON output for memory purge
tasks.summary: Add stable machine-readable output for `covenant memory purge --json` so maintenance automation can compact memory retention without parsing human text.
expectedFailureModes: Retention automation parses `purged N record(s)` and breaks when wording changes.
`--json` omits the effective cutoff or tier, making memory maintenance receipts hard to correlate.
Live coverage never exercises memory retention through a real daemon and CLI boundary.
verification: cd agent-os && cargo test -p covenant --locked memory_purge_json
cd agent-os && cargo test -p covenantd --test live_cli_memory_purge_json --locked -- --ignored live_
tasks.nextAction: Add `memory purge --json`, include tier/cutoff in the JSON object, and add live CLI retention coverage.

tasks.title: Add JSON output for peer purge
tasks.summary: Add stable machine-readable output for `covenant peers purge --json` so peer-registry retention can run without parsing human text.
expectedFailureModes: Retention automation parses `purged N revoked peer(s)` and breaks when wording changes.
`--json` omits the effective cutoff, making peer-retention receipts hard to correlate.
Live peer coverage exercises list and revoke paths but never purges revoked tombstones through the real CLI.
verification: cd agent-os && cargo test -p covenant --locked peers_purge_json
cd agent-os && cargo test -p covenantd --test live_cli_peers_purge_json --locked -- --ignored live_
tasks.nextAction: Add `peers purge --json`, include cutoff and purged count, and add live CLI peer-retention coverage.

tasks.title: Add JSON output for A2A compaction
tasks.summary: Add stable machine-readable output for `covenant a2a compact --json` so queue-maintenance automation can compact resolved A2A events without parsing human text.
expectedFailureModes: Maintenance automation parses `dropped N a2a event(s)` and breaks when wording changes.
`--json` emits multiple values or mixes human text with JSON stdout.
Live A2A coverage exercises status and repair paths but never compacts through the real CLI boundary.
verification: cd agent-os && cargo test -p covenant --locked a2a_compact_json
cd agent-os && cargo test -p covenantd --test live_cli_a2a_compact_json --locked -- --ignored live_
tasks.nextAction: Add `a2a compact --json`, emit dropped count as one object, and add live CLI coverage.

tasks.title: Add JSON output for memory reads
tasks.summary: Add stable machine-readable output for `covenant memory recent --json` and `covenant memory search --json` so agents can inspect memory without parsing display lines.
expectedFailureModes: Automation parses `[timestamp] tier: text` display rows and breaks when formatting changes.
`--json` emits multiple records instead of one envelope with the applied filters.
Search JSON omits the query or effective tier/limit, making memory-read evidence hard to replay.
verification: cd agent-os && cargo test -p covenant --locked memory_read_json
cd agent-os && cargo test -p covenantd --test live_cli_memory_read_json --locked -- --ignored live_
tasks.nextAction: Triaged task: add --json to memory recent/search without changing default text output.

tasks.title: Add JSON output for peer token rotation
tasks.summary: Add stable machine-readable output for `covenant peers rotate --json` so operator-token rotation can be automated without parsing two human text lines.
expectedFailureModes: Credential rotation automation scrapes the last stdout line and breaks when human wording changes.
`--json` leaks unrelated peer registry internals instead of returning only the replacement token contract.
Live token-rotation coverage proves IPC rotation but not the real CLI JSON boundary agents depend on.
verification: cd agent-os && cargo test -p covenant --locked peers_rotate_json
cd agent-os && cargo test -p covenantd --test live_cli_peers_rotate_json --locked -- --ignored live_
tasks.nextAction: Triaged task: add --json to peers rotate without changing default human output.

tasks.title: Add JSON output for intent submission
tasks.summary: Add stable machine-readable output for `covenant intent --json <text>` so autonomous callers can capture intent ids, status, result text, sources, and settlement receipts without parsing human stdout.
expectedFailureModes: Automation scrapes the plain result line and loses the daemon-assigned intent id.
`--json` omits status or settlement data needed to correlate memory, audit, and receipt evidence.
CLI live coverage proves text rendering but not the structured automation boundary.
verification: cd agent-os && cargo test -p covenant --locked intent_result_json
cd agent-os && cargo test -p covenantd --test live_cli_intent_json --locked -- --ignored live_
tasks.nextAction: Triaged task: add --json to intent submission without changing default text output.

tasks.title: Add JSON output for daemon ping
tasks.summary: Add stable machine-readable output for `covenant ping --json` so supervisors and agents can probe daemon health without parsing `pong`.
expectedFailureModes: Supervision scripts parse the literal `pong` line and break if human output changes.
`--json` mixes human text with the JSON health envelope.
Live daemon coverage exercises ping but not the real CLI JSON boundary.
verification: cd agent-os && cargo test -p covenant --locked ping_json
cd agent-os && cargo test -p covenantd --test live_cli_ping_json --locked -- --ignored live_
tasks.nextAction: Triaged task: add --json to ping without changing default pong output.

tasks.title: Add JSON output for capability grants
tasks.summary: Add stable machine-readable output for `covenant capabilities grant --json` so delegation setup can capture the granted action and signature without parsing human lines.
expectedFailureModes: Automation scrapes `signature: ...` from human stdout and breaks when wording changes.
`--json` drops the effective action after A2A peer-prefix expansion.
Grant JSON omits scope or expiry values, making delegated permission evidence harder to replay.
verification: cd agent-os && cargo test -p covenant --locked capability_grant_json
cd agent-os && cargo test -p covenantd --test live_cli_capabilities_grant_json --locked -- --ignored live_
tasks.nextAction: Triaged task: add --json to capability grants without changing default human output.

tasks.title: Require neutral current Git identity
tasks.summary: Tighten the active Git identity guard so future autonomous commits use a neutral automation identity instead of account-linked local metadata.
expectedFailureModes: Local git config drifts back to an account-linked identity.
The current-identity guard accepts historical pseudonyms for new commits.
A session can push with an allowed historical author even though the active author should be neutral.
tasks.nextAction: Triaged task: require neutral current Git identity for future autonomous commits.

tasks.title: Add JSON output for capability revocation
tasks.summary: Add stable machine-readable output for `covenant capabilities revoke --json` so delegated permission teardown can record whether a signature was actually removed.
expectedFailureModes: Automation parses `revoked:` or `(no live capability...)` from human stdout.
`--json` loses the removed=false case, making idempotent revoke workflows ambiguous.
Live revoke coverage proves the human path but not the structured automation boundary.
verification: cd agent-os && cargo test -p covenant --locked capability_revoke_json
cd agent-os && cargo test -p covenantd --test live_cli_capabilities_revoke_json --locked -- --ignored live_
tasks.nextAction: Triaged task: add --json to capability revocation without changing default human output.

tasks.title: Add JSON output for CLI tool calls
tasks.summary: Add stable machine-readable output for `covenant tools call --json` so supervisors can invoke tools without parsing mixed text and pretty JSON blocks.
expectedFailureModes: Automation parses plain text or pretty-printed JSON content blocks from stdout.
Tool errors lose their structured content or exit status when called by a supervisor.
Live coverage proves tool listing JSON but not the real CLI tool-call boundary.
verification: cd agent-os && cargo test -p covenant --locked tool_result_json
cd agent-os && cargo test -p covenantd --test live_cli_tools_call_json --locked -- --ignored live_
tasks.nextAction: Triaged task: add --json to CLI tool calls without changing default human output.

tasks.title: Add JSON output for the CLI audit feed
tasks.summary: Add stable machine-readable output for `covenant audit recent --json` so supervisors can consume audit events as one envelope instead of line-oriented JSONL.
expectedFailureModes: Automation must special-case JSONL parsing while most other CLI surfaces emit one JSON object.
Empty audit feeds emit a human marker instead of a structured zero-event result.
Live coverage proves the JSONL audit path but not the structured supervisor path.
verification: cd agent-os && cargo test -p covenant --locked audit_recent_json
cd agent-os && cargo test -p covenantd --test live_cli_audit_recent_json --locked -- --ignored live_
tasks.nextAction: Triaged task: add --json to audit recent while preserving JSONL default output.

tasks.title: Add live repair coverage after verifier drift
tasks.summary: Prove that a drift item reported by `covenant verify --json` can be resolved through the public memory repair CLI and that a follow-up verify run clears the targeted drift.
expectedFailureModes: The verifier reports actionable repair text but the public CLI repair path cannot apply the suggested change.
Repair mutates state but leaves the same drift row visible on the next verify run.
Live coverage proves drift detection without proving a resumable repair loop.
verification: cd agent-os && cargo test -p covenantd --test live_cli_verify_json --locked -- --ignored live_
tasks.nextAction: Seed a verifier drift case with a repairable memory parent issue, apply the memory repair CLI, and assert the targeted verifier drift disappears.

tasks.title: Add live CLI coverage for memory compaction
tasks.summary: Exercise memory compaction through a real daemon and CLI subprocess, covering dry-run and apply behavior plus audit evidence for deleted, marked, and detached records.
expectedFailureModes: Compaction passes unit tests but the public CLI cannot submit the policy shape through IPC.
Dry-run and apply produce inconsistent outcome summaries under the real SQLite memory store.
Compaction removes records without audit evidence that a supervisor can inspect.
verification: cd agent-os && cargo test -p covenantd --test live_cli_memory_compaction --locked -- --ignored live_
tasks.nextAction: Add an ignored live CLI compaction fixture that proves dry-run/apply consistency and updates the memory retention coverage matrix.

tasks.title: Prove ignored intents do not write memory or receipts
tasks.summary: Add a live daemon/CLI fixture showing an intent rejected by ignore policy exits predictably and does not create memory records, receipts, or dispatch audit rows.
expectedFailureModes: The ignore CLI check passes but real dispatch still writes memory for ignored content.
Ignored dispatch exits non-zero but leaves settlement receipts or audit rows that look like accepted work.
Supervisors cannot distinguish ignored work from failed accepted work in live state.
verification: cd agent-os && cargo test -p covenantd --test live_cli_ignore_dispatch --locked -- --ignored live_
tasks.nextAction: Add a live ignored-dispatch fixture and update ignore policy live coverage evidence.

tasks.title: Add live stale-lease guard coverage for A2A repair
tasks.summary: Cover the A2A repair lease guard through real CLI subprocesses so stale or mismatched lease ids cannot requeue the wrong in-flight task.
expectedFailureModes: The stale-lease guard is tested only through in-process daemon helpers, not the public CLI path.
CLI argument parsing sends the wrong lease id or omits the guard and requeues unsafe work.
A failed guard does not produce an operator-visible rejection that automation can classify.
verification: cd agent-os && cargo test -p covenantd --test live_cli_a2a_repair --locked -- --ignored live_
tasks.nextAction: Extend the live A2A repair fixture with a stale lease rejection before any successful requeue path.

tasks.title: Define the alpha release contract
tasks.summary: Define what an alpha release must truthfully include before Covenant is presented as installable agent-native operating-layer infrastructure.
expectedFailureModes: The project claims alpha readiness without naming supported platforms, commands, or known unsafe edges.
Release docs imply sandbox, settlement, or provenance guarantees that are still experimental.
Contributors cannot tell which gaps block an alpha tag versus later research work.
humanEscalation: Human approval before tagging or publishing an actual release artifact
tasks.nextAction: Write the alpha release contract, mark unsupported claims explicitly, and separate release blockers from post-alpha research.

tasks.title: Cover scoped audit purge rejection live path
tasks.summary: Add live CLI/daemon coverage proving an `audit.purge` grant with a scoped cutoff rejects purge requests beyond that cutoff and preserves audit state.
expectedFailureModes: Unit tests enforce purge cutoff scope but public CLI dispatch accepts an out-of-scope cutoff.
Rejected purge requests mutate audit state before returning an error.
Operator-facing output does not let automation classify a scope rejection.
verification: cd agent-os && cargo test -p covenantd --test live_cli_audit_purge_json --locked -- --ignored live_
tasks.nextAction: Extend the live audit purge JSON fixture with scoped rejection and state-preservation assertions.

tasks.title: Cover scoped capability purge rejection live path
tasks.summary: Add live CLI coverage proving scoped `capabilities.purge` retention limits reject excessive purge windows and preserve capability state.
expectedFailureModes: Dispatch-time scope tests pass in-process but public CLI purge still accepts out-of-scope cutoffs.
A rejected purge deletes capability rows before returning an error.
Automation cannot distinguish a scope rejection from a parse or daemon failure.
verification: cd agent-os && cargo test -p covenantd --test live_cli_capabilities_purge_json --locked -- --ignored live_
tasks.nextAction: Extend the live capabilities purge fixture with scoped rejection and no-mutation assertions.

tasks.title: Add live HTTP mutation coverage
tasks.summary: Add live HTTP coverage for a high-risk protected mutation endpoint using bearer auth, asserting success and rejection behavior match IPC/CLI semantics.
expectedFailureModes: HTTP accepts a protected mutation without the same capability checks as IPC.
Bearer-auth mutation behavior diverges from the socket path.
The live coverage matrix keeps treating HTTP as health/version/tool-call only after mutation coverage exists.
verification: cd agent-os && cargo test -p covenantd --test live_http_gateway --locked -- --ignored live_
tasks.nextAction: Extend HTTP live coverage to one protected mutation endpoint and update matrix/docs.

tasks.title: Correlate memory records with local receipts
tasks.summary: Add an explicit memory-record correlation field to local settlement receipts so verifiers and operators can join memory writes to receipts without relying on ordering or audit inference.
expectedFailureModes: Memory and receipt drift reports cannot identify which receipt belongs to which memory record.
Adding receipt metadata breaks backward-compatible receipt reads.
Docs claim exact reconciliation while the receipt schema still lacks a memory id.
tasks.nextAction: Design and implement a backward-compatible receipt correlation field for memory writes, then update verifier/docs.

tasks.title: Add local model availability probes
tasks.summary: Add explicit local model availability probes so opt-in Ollama live tests report missing models clearly before expanding model coverage.
expectedFailureModes: Live Ollama tests fail with generic connection or model errors that look like code regressions.
Contributors cannot preflight required local models before running live coverage.
Model-dependent release evidence is treated as skipped without a machine-readable reason.
tasks.nextAction: Add a model availability probe command or script plus docs linking it from live coverage.

tasks.title: Add alpha release evidence helper
tasks.summary: Add a deterministic read-only helper that prints alpha validation commands, current commit, dirty-state status, and unsupported external-service notes without tagging or publishing.
expectedFailureModes: Release evidence is collected manually and misses required alpha gates.
A helper intended for evidence accidentally tags or publishes artifacts.
Evidence output includes machine-local paths or personal identity metadata.
humanEscalation: Human approval is required before tagging or publishing release artifacts.
tasks.nextAction: Add a read-only alpha release evidence helper and document it without creating a release.

tasks.title: Define A2A retry idempotency policy
tasks.summary: Define the idempotency metadata and operator policy required before automatic A2A retry can be implemented.
expectedFailureModes: Automatic retry work begins before task classes can declare duplicate safety.
Requeue policy hides duplicate-work risk from operators.
Docs imply retries are safe while only manual repair is implemented.
tasks.nextAction: Write the A2A idempotency policy and convert automatic retry into concrete implementation tasks.

tasks.title: Define release artifact provenance subjects
tasks.summary: Extend provenance planning for release artifact subjects so future signed releases can bind tag, commit, artifacts, checksums, and validation evidence without choosing key custody yet.
expectedFailureModes: Release provenance binds commits and tasks but not artifacts.
Key custody decisions block schema work that can be designed independently.
Docs imply signed releases before artifact-subject schema exists.
humanEscalation: Human decision remains required for public signing keys and release publication.
tasks.nextAction: Define release artifact subject schema and update provenance docs, leaving key custody as human-governed.
